name: Oracle Health Foundation — Pediatric Medical Grants
description: The Oracle Health Foundation provides grants for pediatric medical care to children in need around the world. The foundation offers financial support for clinical treatment, medical equipment, and travel/lodging related to accessing pediatric healthcare. Pediatric grants cover a wide range of conditions and treatment needs, with dedicated case managers guiding families through the application process. The program is particularly valuable for immigrant and refugee families whose children need specialized medical treatment not available in their home countries or who face financial barriers to accessing care. Grants do not exceed $17,000 for clinical and equipment requests (averaging approximately $2,500 per case) and do not exceed $1,000 for travel and lodging requests. The foundation works with healthcare facilities globally to ensure children receive necessary medical interventions.
eligibility: Children in need of pediatric medical care worldwide; families must demonstrate financial need and medical necessity; open to international patients including immigrant and refugee children
amount: Up to $17,000 for clinical and equipment requests (average $2,500); up to $1,000 for travel and lodging
targetDiagnosis: Various pediatric conditions requiring specialized treatment
applicationProcess: Submit a grant request through the Oracle Health Foundation website. Applications are reviewed by case managers who assess medical necessity and financial need. Required documentation includes medical records, treatment plan from a healthcare provider, and proof of financial hardship. Case managers are available to assist families throughout the application process.
geographicScope: International — grants available for children worldwide, including those receiving care outside of the United States and Canada
documentsRequired: Medical records; treatment plan from a qualified healthcare provider; proof of financial need; identification documents for the child and parent/guardian

name: RDCRN — Rare Diseases Clinical Research Network Grants
organization: NIH / Rare Diseases Clinical Research Network
description: The Rare Diseases Clinical Research Network (RDCRN), funded by the National Institutes of Health, operates 21 research consortia focused on over 200 rare diseases. Each consortium, in partnership with affiliated patient advocacy groups, offers various funding opportunities including early career research grants, biomarker development programs, clinical research training scholarships, and young investigator awards. The RDCRN facilitates collaboration among researchers, patients, and advocacy organizations to advance understanding and treatment of rare diseases. International researchers and patients can participate in RDCRN clinical studies conducted across multiple sites in the United States and globally. For immigrants and international patients with rare diseases, the RDCRN provides access to cutting-edge clinical trials and research studies that may not be available in their home countries.
eligibility: Researchers, clinicians, and patients involved in rare disease research; early career investigators; international collaboration welcome through consortium partnerships; patients with qualifying rare diseases may participate in clinical trials
amount: Varies by consortium and grant type — early career grants typically $40,000–$150,000 per year; patient travel support available for clinical trial participants
targetDiagnosis: Over 200 rare diseases across 21 consortia including rare neurological, immunological, metabolic, and genetic conditions
applicationProcess: Visit the RDCRN website to identify the consortium relevant to your rare disease condition. Each consortium publishes its own funding announcements with specific deadlines and application procedures. Researchers apply through the consortium's designated application portal. Patients interested in clinical trial participation can search for active studies through the RDCRN patient contact registry.
geographicScope: United States — with international collaboration sites; 21 consortia operating across multiple clinical sites
documentsRequired: For researchers: CV, research proposal, institutional support letter, IRB approval; for patients: medical documentation of rare disease diagnosis, referral from treating physician

name: FDA Rare Disease Research — Novel Approaches for Ultra-Rare Cancers
description: The FDA's funding program for Novel Approaches to Support Therapeutic Development in Ultra-Rare Cancers provides grants to fund research developing new approaches for drug development in ultra-rare pediatric and adult cancers. The program specifically targets areas where there is little economic incentive for commercial entities to conduct the research, making it a critical source of funding for conditions that pharmaceutical companies may overlook. This initiative supports studies that develop methodologies, tools, and frameworks to overcome the unique challenges of clinical development for cancers affecting very small patient populations. International patients and researchers can benefit from the research outcomes, and the program advances global understanding of ultra-rare malignancies. For immigrant families with children or relatives diagnosed with ultra-rare cancers, this program can help accelerate access to experimental treatments through clinical trial pathways.
eligibility: Academic researchers, clinical investigators, and institutions studying ultra-rare cancers; focus on pediatric and adult ultra-rare malignancies with limited commercial development interest; U.S.-based institutions with international collaboration possible
amount: Varies by funding cycle — typically $200,000–$500,000 per project over 2–3 years
targetDiagnosis: Ultra-rare pediatric and adult cancers with limited therapeutic options
applicationProcess: Monitor the FDA CDER Funding Opportunities page for open solicitations. Submit proposals through the designated application portal (typically grants.gov) during the open application period. Proposals should describe novel methodologies for supporting drug development in ultra-rare cancers. Peer review is conducted by FDA and external experts.
geographicScope: United States — with potential international research collaboration; outcomes benefit the global rare cancer community
documentsRequired: Research proposal; institutional credentials; investigator CV and track record; budget justification; IRB approval or plan; letters of collaboration if applicable

name: Fondation Maladies Rares — Rare Disease Scientific Research Grants
organization: Fondation Maladies Rares (Foundation for Rare Diseases)
description: The Fondation Maladies Rares (Foundation for Rare Diseases) is a French foundation that funds scientific research projects focused on rare diseases. The foundation provides grants to researchers and research teams working to advance diagnosis, treatment, and understanding of the approximately 7,000 known rare diseases. Funded projects span translational research, clinical studies, genetic analysis, and therapeutic development. The foundation collaborates with European research networks including ERDERA and supports international scientific collaboration. For immigrants in France and Europe diagnosed with rare conditions, this foundation's work drives access to novel diagnostics and experimental treatments. The foundation also supports patient registries and natural history studies that help rare disease patients access appropriate care regardless of their country of origin.
eligibility: Researchers and research teams at French or European institutions working on rare disease projects; international collaboration encouraged; projects must focus on rare diseases as defined by European prevalence criteria (fewer than 1 in 2,000 people affected)
amount: Varies by call — typically €20,000–€50,000 per project; larger collaborative grants available
targetDiagnosis: All rare diseases (approximately 7,000 recognized conditions) — genetic, metabolic, neurological, immunological, and oncological rare diseases
applicationProcess: Monitor the Foundation's website for open calls for proposals. Submit a research project application during the open submission period. Applications undergo scientific peer review. Selected projects receive funding disbursed through the applicant's research institution. The foundation publishes annual calls covering different thematic areas of rare disease research.
geographicScope: France and Europe — research institutions in France preferred, with European and international collaboration supported
documentsRequired: Research proposal; CV of principal investigator; institutional affiliation letter; budget plan; ethics committee approval if applicable; description of expected patient impact
